134	`systemd --user` unit (`systemd/claude-slack-bot.service`). Restart-on-failure baked in. Logs:
135

138	```
139	
140	## Implemented features
141	
142	- HTTP event endpoint at `http://127.0.0.1:8787/event`
143	- SQLite-backed session/event registry
144	- Slack Socket Mode listener (no inbound port required)
145	- Top-level message per named session, thread per session lifetime
146	- Codex/Gemini auto-registration with names like `codex-project-abcdef12`
147	- Portable Codex rename prompt: `rn my-session`
148	- Agent labels in Slack messages: `[Claude]`, `[Codex]`, `[Gemini]`

1	"""Pure functions that turn structured events into Slack message text."""
2	
3	from __future__ import annotations
4	
5	import re
6	from typing import Any
7	
8	_RN_PATTERN = re.compile(r"^(?:(?:[/#!](?:rn|rename|register))|rn)\s+(\S+)\s*$")
9	_TRUNCATE_AT = 3000
10	
11	
12	def agent_label(agent: str | None) -> str:
13	    labels = {
14	        "claude": "Claude",
15	        "codex": "Codex",
16	        "gemini": "Gemini",
17	    }
18	    return labels.get((agent or "claude").lower(), "Claude")
19	
20	
21	def top_level_text(name: str, cwd: str, status: str, agent: str | None = None) -> str:
22	    prefix = f"[{agent_label(agent)}] "
23	    if status == "active":
24	        return f"🟢 {prefix}{name}  ·  {cwd}"
25	    return f"⚪ {prefix}{name}  ·  {cwd}  (ended)"
26	
27	
28	def _codeblock_if_multiline(text: str) -> str:
29	    if "\n" in text:
30	        truncated = text if len(text) <= _TRUNCATE_AT else text[:_TRUNCATE_AT] + "\n…[truncated]"
31	        return f"\n```\n{truncated}\n```"
32	    return f" {text}"
33	
34	
35	def format_event(kind: str, data: dict[str, Any]) -> str:
36	    prefix = f"[{agent_label(str(data.get('agent', 'claude')))}] "
37	    if kind == "prompt":
38	        return f"{prefix}👤{_codeblock_if_multiline(str(data.get('text', '')))}"
39	    if kind == "response":
40	        body = f"{prefix}🤖{_codeblock_if_multiline(str(data.get('text', '')))}"
41	        summary = data.get("tool_summary")
42	        if summary:
43	            body += f"\n_↳ {summary}_"
44	        return body
45	    if kind == "notification":
46	        return f"{prefix}⏸ {data.get('message', '')}"
47	    if kind == "error":
48	        return f"{prefix}❌ {data.get('text', '')}"
49	    return f"{prefix}[{kind}] {data!r}"
50	
51	
52	def parse_rn_command(prompt_text: str) -> str | None:
53	    """Return the name argument if `prompt_text` is a rename command."""
54	    m = _RN_PATTERN.match(prompt_text.strip())
55	    return m.group(1) if m else None

content.text:
Yes — works for any question. The underlying mechanism is just "type your text + Enter into the pane," so whatever input CC accepts at the terminal works:

| CC prompt type | Reply in Slack |
|---|---|
| Permission prompt (3-option default) | `1`/`2`/`3` |
| Multi-choice in assistant text (1-4 or more) | `1`/`2`/`3`/`4` |
| Free-form question | Just type the answer |
| y/n prompt | `y` or `n` |

The **hint** I added ("Reply `1` to approve, `2` to deny, `3` to allow for session") only shows for actual permission prompts because we detect those via the `tool_use` block in the transcript. For general "1-4" questions, those appear in Claude's regular response (mirrored via the Stop hook) — you'll see the question + options in the thread and can just reply with the number.

If you want the hint to be smarter (e.g. detect any `1)` / `2)` pattern in the text and show "Reply with option number" generically), I can add that — small regex in `events.py`. Worth doing, or leave as-is?

1	# claude-slack-bot
2	
3	Bridge between Claude Code, Codex, and Gemini CLI sessions and Slack: mirrors selected agent sessions into Slack threads, and types your Slack replies back into the originating Zellij pane.
4	
5	## What this does
6	
7	Registers Claude sessions with `/rn <name>`, and auto-registers Codex/Gemini sessions because those CLIs do not provide the same custom slash-command path. The bot posts a top-level message naming the session and mirrors every subsequent prompt, response, and notification into the thread beneath it. Replying in that Slack thread types your reply into the originating Zellij pane (via `zellij action write-chars`).
8	
9	## Use cases
10	
11	- Mobile notifications when CC asks for input or finishes a long-running turn
12	- Reply to CC from your phone — text is typed into the live terminal session
13	- Monitor multiple parallel CC sessions from one Slack channel
14	- Long-lived searchable archive of selected bug-bounty sessions
15	
16	## Requirements
17	
18	- Linux or WSL2 (with systemd enabled in `/etc/wsl.conf`)
19	- Python 3.13, `uv`
20	- Zellij ≥ 0.44
21	- `jq`, `curl` (for hook scripts)
22	- A Slack workspace where you can create an app
23	- Claude Code CLI, Codex CLI, or Gemini CLI
24	
25	## Installation / Setup
26	
27	### 1. Create the Slack app
28	
29	1. Visit https://api.slack.com/apps → "Create New App" → "From scratch"
30	2. Name: `claude-slack-bot`; pick your workspace
31	3. **Socket Mode** → enable, generate app-level token (`xapp-...`)
32	4. **OAuth & Permissions** → add bot scopes:
33	   `chat:write`, `chat:write.public`, `channels:history`, `groups:history`,
34	   `reactions:write`, `commands`, `app_mentions:read`
35	5. **Event Subscriptions** → enable, subscribe to bot events: `message.channels`, `message.groups`, `app_mention`
36	6. Install to workspace; copy `xoxb-...` bot token
37	7. Invite the bot to the channel you'll use (e.g. `/invite @claude-slack-bot`)
38	8. Right-click the channel → "Copy link" — the trailing path is the channel ID (`C0123…`)
39	
40	### 2. Create the env file
41	
42	```bash
43	mkdir -p ~/.config/claude-slack-bot
44	cat > ~/.config/claude-slack-bot/env <<'EOF'
45	SLACK_BOT_TOKEN=xoxb-…
46	SLACK_APP_TOKEN=xapp-…
47	SLACK_CHANNEL_ID=C…
48	# Optional: route agents to separate Slack channels. Defaults to SLACK_CHANNEL_ID.
49	# SLACK_CHANNEL_ID_CLAUDE=C…
50	# SLACK_CHANNEL_ID_CODEX=C…
51	# SLACK_CHANNEL_ID_GEMINI=C…
52	SLACKBOT_PORT=8787
53	LOG_LEVEL=INFO
54	EOF
55	chmod 600 ~/.config/claude-slack-bot/env
56	```
57	
58	### 3. Install the daemon
59	
60	```bash
61	cd ~/git/priv/claude-slack-bot
62	uv venv && uv sync

71	
72	### 4. Install the agent hooks
73	
74	```bash
75	bash ~/git/priv/claude-slack-bot/hooks/install.sh
76	bash ~/git/priv/claude-slack-bot/hooks/install-codex.sh
77	bash ~/git/priv/claude-slack-bot/hooks/install-gemini.sh

81	
82	- Claude: `~/.claude/settings.json`
83	- Codex: `~/.codex/hooks.json`
84	- Gemini: `~/.gemini/settings.json`

88	## Usage
89	
90	1. Start your agent inside a Zellij pane
91	2. Claude: run `/rn my-session`; Codex/Gemini: the thread appears automatically
92	3. Codex: optionally rename the thread with `rn my-session`; the hook blocks that control prompt from reaching the model
93	4. Type prompts in the agent; they mirror into the Slack thread
94	5. From Slack (mobile or desktop), reply in the thread — the text is typed into the agent pane (the pane briefly takes focus)

97	
98	```bash

100	uv run pytest -v
101	uv run ruff check . && uv run ruff format --check .
102	shellcheck hooks/*.sh
103	```

112	  http://127.0.0.1:8787/event

131	
132	## Deployment
133	
134	`systemd --user` unit (`systemd/claude-slack-bot.service`). Restart-on-failure baked in. Logs:

144	- Slack Socket Mode listener (no inbound port required)

Triggers on tasks like "write a probe", "bash wrapper", "heredoc with curl", "recon one-liner", "TSV parser", "for-each host in a list", or any shell snippet longer than 3 lines or with more than 2 pipes. - update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- verify: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by running the app and observing behavior. Use when asked to verify a PR, confirm a fix works, test a change manually, check that a feature works, or validate local changes before pushing.
- code-review: Review the current diff for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings). Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the current diff and apply the fixes — equivalent to /code-review --fix.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Build, debug, and optimize Claude API / Anthropic SDK apps. Apps built with this skill should include prompt caching. Also handles migrating existing Claude API code between Claude model versions (4.5 → 4.6, 4.6 → 4.7, retired-model replacements).
TRIGGER when: code imports `anthropic`/`@anthropic-ai/sdk`; user asks for the Claude API, Anthropic SDK, or Managed Agents; user adds/modifies/tunes a Claude feature (caching, thinking, compaction, tool use, batch, files, citations, memory) or model (Opus/Sonnet/Haiku) in a file; questions about prompt caching / cache hit rate in an Anthropic SDK project.
SKIP: file imports `openai`/other-provider SDK, filename like `*-openai.py`/`*-generic.py`, provider-neutral code, general programming/ML.
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests).
